reconcile.note: Gill reads 'the twelve' in 1 Corinthians 15:5 as the apostles' retained title of office, not a literal headcount, noting some manuscripts read 'the eleven' instead.

discrepancy.note: Strauss flags the headcount tension directly: Luke's eleven, John's ten, and Paul's twelve cannot all describe the same post-resurrection body without loss.

quotes.text: the eleven of Luke, as at variance with the statement of John that only ten apostles were present, any more than the twelve of Paul, from which number Judas at least must be deducted
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, Part III, ch. 3 (1846), on Matthew 28:16 and 1 Corinthians 15:5.

sides.snippet: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee
sides.verseText: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
